top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the invention and realization of the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye, a cleanly bounded, two-name allocation with a quantitative, reproduced result (frequency measurement near 1e-18) and a citation that names magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, which distinguishes it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It is the most mature and defensible discovery-or-invention case. P002 follows because moire quantum matter is a genuine new-phase discovery, but the three-name allocation omits Yuan Cao and early groups and the superconductivity interpretation is less settled; both still rank above no award, since a defensible laureate case exists.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; long-running academic exchanges with Japanese universities (including a University of Tokyo fellowship) are a field-level connection only, with no documented tie to Katori or Ye, and Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, which concerns committee composition and no candidate
